title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Make SPACE to disciple someone. Learn from Jesus and Paul, then use a simple four-step process to help another person grow in love for God and others and eventually disciple someone else.

blocks.text: Growing Deep helped you become rooted in the gospel. Growing Up showed you how to love others, and Growing Out has helped you pray, serve, and share Jesus. Now comes a beautiful next step: helping another person grow. A healthy tree bears fruit, and over time one tree can become an orchard.

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
When Paul met Timothy in Lystra, Timothy was already a disciple with a good reputation among the believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul invited him to travel and serve alongside him. Timothy heard Paul teach and watched how he lived through hardship. Years later Paul reminded him, "You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness" (2 Timothy 3:10).

Paul did more than give Timothy information. He shared his life and prepared Timothy to lead. Even when they were apart, Paul wrote to instruct and encourage him. Then Paul gave Timothy a charge that reached far beyond the two of them.
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

Notice the four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. Paul was not trying to make Timothy depend on him forever. He wanted Timothy to pass on what he had received. Someone helped you follow Jesus. Who might God use you to help?
8.1 - Who has helped you grow in love for God and others? What did that person do?
Jesus Calls Ordinary People to Make Disciples

Jesus chose twelve disciples "so that they might be with him" (Mark 3:14). Before they were sent out, they spent time with Him. They heard His teaching, watched His compassion, and saw Him pray. Jesus also gave them opportunities to serve. When the apostles returned from being sent out, they told Him what they had done and taught (Mark 6:30). He was forming people who would carry His message to others.

Jesus later commanded His followers to make disciples, baptizing them and "teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:19-20). The goal is not simply that someone knows more Bible facts. Discipleship helps a person grow in love for God and love for others, and learn to obey Jesus in everyday life.

Perhaps you feel unqualified. You still have questions. You still struggle with sin. So did the people Jesus first called. You do not need to be a perfect Christian or have every answer. You need to keep following Jesus, care about another person, and be willing to share what you are learning. Jesus ends the Great Commission with a promise: "I am with you always" (Matthew 28:20).
Make SPACE to Disciple Someone

Discipleship grows through an intentional relationship. It gives someone room to ask honest questions, face struggles, practice obedience, and celebrate progress. Make SPACE to disciple someone: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage. These are four things you can actually do. You can return to them again and again as a person grows.
S: Study

Open God's Word and learn. Ask, "Would you like to do a Bible study with me?" Growing Together gives you a path to follow. Start with the lessons that fit the person's needs, whether that means the foundations in 101 or a topic from the 200 series. Read the lesson, look at Scripture, ask what it means, and pray. The goal is not to finish pages. It is to help someone know Jesus and love Him more.
P: Practice

Learning becomes stronger when someone can try what they have learned. Model the skill first, then invite them to practice in a safe setting. After a lesson about sharing the gospel, you might say, "Let's practice sharing your testimony. You can share yours with me." Later, invite them to lead a question or explain a Bible passage. You can prepare with them beforehand. They learn by watching, trying, and trying again.
AC: Appropriate Challenge

Give a specific next step that fits the person's readiness. You might say, "I want to challenge you to start a conversation about Jesus with someone this week." A newer believer may be ready to pray aloud or share a testimony. Someone with more experience may be ready to lead part of a Growing Together lesson. Eventually, the challenge may be, "Would you invite someone to begin this study with you?" A good challenge stretches someone without leaving them on their own.
E: Encourage

Follow up with care. Ask what happened, listen, pray, and celebrate the courage it took to try. You might say, "I'm so proud of you for taking that step. How did it go?" If the person struggled, encourage them without pretending it was easy. Help them learn and choose another step. Paul continued to teach and strengthen Timothy through his letters. Encouragement is not an extra after the real work. It is part of helping someone grow.

The wheel is a reminder of what you are helping someone grow in: Christ at the center, with Scripture, prayer, fellowship, witness, and obedience shaping daily life. SPACE is the process you use to help them grow in those areas. You can study a truth, practice it, offer an appropriate challenge, and encourage the person afterward.
8.2 - Think of one area where a friend could grow in love for God or others. How could you use Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, and Encourage to help?
From Learner to Disciple-Maker

The process grows with the person. At first, you may lead most of a Growing Together lesson while the other person listens and asks questions. Soon, invite them to prepare and lead a small section. Practice with them before they lead. Give an appropriate challenge, then ask how it went and encourage them. Over time, let them take more responsibility.

One day the next appropriate challenge may be to begin studying with someone else. They can use the same Growing Together lessons and the same SPACE process. You are not handing them a title or asking them to become an expert. You are helping them care for another person the way someone cared for them. That is the movement of 2 Timothy 2:2: faithful people learning to teach others.

Who should you invite? Paul told Timothy to entrust the message to faithful people. Look for someone who is faithful, available, and teachable. They do not need to know much or look impressive. They need a willingness to learn and make room for growth. Begin with one person, not a complicated program. Ask whether they would like to work through a study with you, perhaps once a week or every other week.
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person you could invite to study Growing Together with you?
God Gives the Growth

Think of an orchard. A gardener can prepare the soil, plant, water, and care for a young tree. But the gardener cannot make it live. Paul wrote, "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth" (1 Corinthians 3:6). Your job is not to change another person's heart. Only God can do that. Your part is to love, open His Word, model obedience, give wise challenges, encourage, and depend on the Holy Spirit.

This is why discipleship takes patience. Some conversations will feel fruitful. Others will feel slow. Keep praying and keep caring. The aim is not to produce a person who can repeat your answers. It is to help someone love Jesus and others more deeply, serve in His church, and eventually help another person do the same.
8.4 - What might keep you from inviting someone to study with you, and what is one small step you could take this week?
Lesson 8 Review

Jesus calls His followers to make disciples, and Paul showed Timothy how faith can be passed from one generation to the next. You can make SPACE to disciple someone: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage. Use Growing Together as a guide, share your life, and help the person take increasing responsibility until they can disciple someone else. God gives the growth, and Jesus promises to be with you.
In the next lesson, you will consider the people God places beside you in His mission, from your church to the ends of the earth.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
